title: hace = ago, responder, mes; you: -aste / -iste; they: -aron / -ieron; anoche

cards.title: hace = ago
cards.body: 'It makes two weeks' = two weeks ago.

examples.en: I saw him two weeks ago.

cards.title: responder; 'I answered her (the) mail'
cards.body: Spanish uses fewer possessives: 'I answered her it' instead of 'I answered her email'. Mes (month) is masculine.

examples.en: I answered her seven weeks ago.
I answered it (her email) a month ago.
examples.es: Se lo respondí hace un mes.

cards.title: Recap: discriminé, discriminó, discriminamos
cards.body: Read the vowels as written: discriminación has an i.

cards.title: you (informal): -aste / -iste
cards.body: Anoche = last night. Don't confuse it with esta noche (tonight).

examples.en: Didn't you go out last night?

cards.title: viviste vs vivías
cards.body: Often both work; the difference is whether you picture a closed period or an ongoing one.

examples.en: Where did you live? / Where were you living?

cards.title: esperaste, llegaste
cards.body: 'When did you arrive?' is clearly a point in time.

examples.en: Why didn't you wait for me?

cards.title: The full dot past — and its i
cards.body: In the present, -er/-ir verbs are dominated by e (with i only in -imos). In the dot past it's the reverse: i everywhere, e only in -ieron.

practice.en: I saw him two weeks ago.
I answered her seven weeks ago.
I answered it (her email) a month ago.
